evals.prompt: Plan a behavior-preserving Rust refactor of a parser that mixes IO and parsing. Coverage is weak, callers depend on typed errors and stable output ordering, and I am not asking for commits.
evals.expected_output: A smell-led, reversible refactoring sequence with characterization tests, explicit behavior surface, Rust-aware mechanics, green checkpoints, and no unsolicited commits.
expectations: Positive: establishes a green baseline and characterization tests for typed errors, ordering, and current edge behavior before moving code.
Names small reversible refactorings and assigns focused checks plus broader green checkpoints instead of demanding the full suite after every edit.
Preserves Result variants/source semantics and deterministic output, and uses a rollback mechanism without creating commits.

evals.prompt: While renaming the invoice module, also add partial refunds and change the public error response to include a new code.
evals.expected_output: A two-hats scope correction that separates behavior-preserving structure work from feature/API changes.
expectations: Negative: does not label partial refunds or a changed public error contract as refactoring.
Separates the work into a green refactoring sequence and a separately tested feature/API migration.

evals.prompt: For speed, replace BTreeMap with HashMap, parallelize iteration, turn panic into Result, extract a Send + Sync trait beside the implementation, and remove pass-through layers. Treat all of this as one refactor.
evals.expected_output: A correction that distinguishes unmeasured optimization and behavior/API changes from safe structural refactoring.
expectations: Corrected behavior: requires a representative workload, baseline/profile, controlled repeated measurements, and a stated metric before performance edits.
Flags ordering, tie-breaking, parallel reduction, panic-versus-Result, error variants, and auto-trait bounds as observable behavior or compatibility concerns.
Places an earned minimal trait with the policy-side consumer and chooses concrete/generic/dyn/enum dispatch from requirements rather than speculative speed.
Removes a layer only when measured overhead matters and the layer hides no valuable policy.
